ingestion.notes: The perturbation and infection results sections were skimmed. Markers are listed as given in the paper; the reference is murine (mouse gene case), and human data are projected via orthologs.

enhanced_abstract.tldr: ProjecTILs projects new T cell scRNA-seq data onto a fixed, annotated reference atlas of tumor-infiltrating T cell states without distorting it, labels each cell by nearest neighbors (91.6% correct in cross-validation), and flags query cells that deviate from known states.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: T cell subtypes and states are defined inconsistently across studies, so results from different datasets, diseases and species are hard to compare.

sections.heading: Reference atlases
sections.body: A murine TIL atlas of 16,803 T cells from 25 samples across six studies (melanoma and colon adenocarcinoma tumors plus tumor-draining lymph nodes), integrated with STACAS. It has nine states: CD8 naive-like, early-activation, effector-memory, precursor-exhausted (Tpex) and terminally exhausted (Tex); CD4 naive-like, Th1-like, Tfh and Treg. A second atlas covers virus-specific CD8 T cells in acute and chronic LCMV infection.

sections.heading: Projection algorithm
sections.body: The query is log-normalized, non-T cells are removed with TILPRED, and the query is batch-aligned to the reference with STACAS/Seurat anchors. The reference's own PCA rotation and UMAP model are then applied to the query, so the reference map never changes. A nearest-neighbor majority vote in PCA or UMAP space assigns each query cell a state. ICA components and discriminant genes reveal programs where the query deviates from the reference.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: In leave-samples-out cross-validation, 90% of projected cells landed within one UMAP unit of their true position and 91.6% got the right state. Tumor-specific OVA-tetramer+ CD8 T cells projected mostly to Tex (90.2%), as expected.

sections.heading: Human tumors
sections.body: Human TILs from melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, breast, liver, lung and colorectal cohorts, projected through mouse orthologs, showed the same subtypes in both species. Expanded, tumor-specific clones sat in Tex, Tpex and part of the effector-memory compartment, supporting a model in which EM cells give rise to Tpex and then Tex.

key_findings: Reference projection keeps the annotated map stable, so different studies can be compared on the same coordinates
T cell subtypes in tumors are conserved across cohorts, cancer types and between human and mouse
Tpex vs. Tex is defined by TCF7/IL7R/XCL1-high, low-cytotoxicity Tpex versus GZMB/PRF1-high, HAVCR2-high proliferating Tex
limitations: Reference atlases are murine; human data go through ortholog mapping
Covers T cells only; other cell types must be filtered out first
Cells in states absent from the reference can only be flagged as deviating, not named
enhanced_abstract.why_it_matters: Rule 3 (algorithm, preferred). A reference-projection method built specifically for T cells in tumors, one of the group's two focus lineages, with explicit marker definitions for each T cell state. CASSIA also uses its T cell reference as a hard benchmark for fine T cell states.

sequencing.summary: New scRNA-seq of T cells from MC38 tumor-draining lymph nodes; otherwise public mouse and human datasets.

quantification.summary: Uses published count matrices; accepts UMI counts or TPM.

preprocessing.summary: Log-normalization log(1 + 10,000·x/S); TILPRED removes non-T cells; variable genes exclude cell-cycle, mitochondrial, ribosomal and non-coding genes.

dimensionality_reduction.summary: The reference's PCA rotation and UMAP model are applied to the query so it lands in the unchanged reference space; ICA (50 components) is used to find gene programs where the query deviates.

batch_correction.summary: STACAS (anchor-based, built on Seurat) integrates studies to build the atlases and aligns each query to the reference before projection.

clustering.summary: SNN clustering of the integrated reference, then manual annotation of clusters into functional states.

annotation.summary: Nearest-neighbor majority vote against the annotated reference assigns each query cell one of nine T cell states; reference states were defined by marker expression, expression gradients and MAST enrichment. Compared with Azimuth, scmap and SingleR.

trajectory.summary: TCR clonal sharing is used to infer a differentiation path (effector-memory → Tpex → Tex), but no trajectory algorithm is run.

algorithms.name: ProjecTILs projection
algorithms.description: Batch-align query to reference, apply reference PCA/UMAP transforms, classify by nearest neighbors.
